title.zh: 中药面膜美容：古方养颜的智慧
title.en: Herbal Mask Beauty: Ancient Wisdom for Skin Care

description.zh: 掌握中药面膜的制作和使用方法，用古方养颜智慧呵护肌肤
description.en: Master herbal mask making and usage, use ancient wisdom for skincare

zh.text: 中药面膜是中医外治法在美容领域的重要应用，有着悠久的历史和深厚的理论基础。《神农本草经》中收录了大量可用于外用的美容中药，而唐代《千金要方》和《外台秘要》中更是详细记载了以白芷、白术、白茯苓等本草调配的"洗面方"和"敷面方"。这些古方流传千年至今，并非因为它们来自"古代"就天然高贵，而是因为其背后的配伍理念——根据皮肤问题的中医病机来选择不同的本草，辨证施治——这才是中药面膜真正的智慧所在。
中药面膜的优势

与市售的化学合成面膜相比，中药面膜有几点突出的优势。其一，天然安全——中药面膜以天然本草为原料，不含化学防腐剂、香精和色素，对皮肤的刺激性小。其二，温和养肤——中药成分通过皮肤吸收，药性平和，不会像某些化学焕肤成分那样剥脱角质、损伤屏障。其三，标本兼治——中药面膜并非单纯遮盖问题，而是根据皮肤问题的中医病机（如热毒、血瘀、湿浊等）选择对应的本草，从根本上改善皮肤状态。其四，个性化调配——可以根据每个人的体质、肤质和具体问题灵活调整配方，真正实现因人而异的养肤。当然，中药面膜也有其局限——起效相对缓慢，需要坚持使用才能看到明显改善，这是本草温和特点所决定的。
经典中药面膜方
流传下来的古代美容方中，有几个至今仍在广泛使用并被现代实践验证有效的经典方子，值得了解。
玉容散

玉容散是古代宫廷美容的代表性方剂，最早记载于《千金要方》。其组成以白芷、白术、白茯苓、白芍等"白色"药材为主，中医取"以色补色"之理，白色入肺，肺主皮毛，故白药有美白肌肤之功。我在临床中常用玉容散化裁，研极细末后调水或蜂蜜做面膜。其中白芷辛温芳香，能"长肌肤、润泽颜色"（《神农本草经》），是玉容散中的核心药物。白芷所含的呋喃香豆素类成分具有光敏活性，因此使用含白芷的面膜后要注意避光防晒，否则反而会引起色素沉着，这一点在临床上必须反复强调。
三白粉面膜
三白粉由白芷、白术、白茯苓三味等份研末而成，是美白养颜最基础的经典方。白芷美白润肤，白术健脾燥湿，白茯苓健脾利湿。三药合用，着眼于"脾主运化"和"肺主皮毛"两大系统——脾气健运则湿浊不生，皮肤自然干净透亮；肺气得宣则皮毛得以润泽。我在实际使用中常建议患者根据皮肤类型选择调液——干性皮肤用蜂蜜调，油性皮肤用牛奶或酸奶调，中性皮肤用清水或花水调，灵活变通效果更佳。
珍珠粉面膜
珍珠粉在中医美容中地位尊崇。《本草纲目》记载珍珠"涂面，令人润泽好颜色；涂手足，去皮肤逆胪"。珍珠的主要成分是碳酸钙和多种氨基酸，外用有良好的吸附和滋养作用。我常遇到患者询问"是不是越贵的珍珠粉效果越好"，其实从药用角度来说，关键不在于价格而在于粉末的细度——珍珠粉越细，越容易被皮肤吸收利用。选购时应以"手捻如面、入水即化"为度。珍珠粉配伍三白粉或单用均可，适合希望美白且皮肤偏敏感的人群。
功能性中药面膜
针对不同的皮肤问题，中药面膜也可以像方剂一样灵活组方，做到"一肤一方"。以下介绍几种我在临床上常用的功能性面膜配方。
美白面膜

zh.title: 美白淡斑面膜
zh.instructions:
1. 将所有粉末混合
2. 加入蜂蜜调成糊状
3. 涂于面部，避开眼周
4. 15-20分钟后洗净
5. 每周2-3次
6. 美白淡斑，提亮肤色

zh.text: 祛痘面膜

zh.title: 清热祛痘面膜
zh.instructions:
1. 将所有粉末混合
2. 加水调成糊状
3. 涂于痘痘部位
4. 10-15分钟后洗净
5. 每周2-3次
6. 清热解毒，祛痘消炎

zh.text: 祛痘面膜的核心在于清热解毒、消肿散结。黄连粉清热燥湿力强，对于红肿热痛的炎性痘痘效果最直接，但因其药性偏寒，不能久敷，10至15分钟即可洗掉。金银花和蒲公英清热解毒、消肿散结，对脓疱型痘痘尤为有效。绿豆粉既有清热解毒之功，又能吸附多余油脂，作为基底粉末非常合适。值得一提的是，祛痘面膜敷用时间不宜过长，因为清热解毒类药物透皮作用较强，敷太久反而可能刺激皮肤。
滋润面膜

zh.title: 滋润养肤面膜
zh.instructions:
1. 将所有粉末混合
2. 加入蜂蜜和牛奶调成糊状
3. 涂于面部
4. 15-20分钟后洗净
5. 每周2-3次
6. 滋润养肤，改善干燥

zh.text: 干燥、脱屑、缺水性皮肤往往不是单纯缺水，而是"血虚风燥"——血虚不能上荣于面，则皮肤失润；血虚生风，风胜则干。当归补血活血，是滋润类面膜的核心；银耳富含天然植物胶质，保湿效果极佳，《本草再新》称其"润肺滋阴"；百合养阴润燥，配合牛奶和蜂蜜的天然保湿因子，形成一层滋润保护膜。建议干性皮肤患者每周使用2至3次，配合口服当归养血食疗，内外同治，效果更持久。
抗衰老面膜

zh.title: 抗衰老养颜面膜
zh.instructions:
1. 将所有粉末混合
2. 加入蜂蜜调成糊状
3. 涂于面部
4. 15-20分钟后洗净
5. 每周1-2次
6. 抗衰老，养颜美容

zh.text: 皮肤老化的中医本质在于气血亏虚、肾精渐衰。人参被誉为"百草之王"，大补元气，外用可增强皮肤活力、延缓胶原流失。当归和枸杞一补血、一滋阴，协同作用。珍珠粉提供皮肤所需氨基酸和微量元素。此方适合35岁以上、开始出现细纹松弛的皮肤使用。不过需注意，人参粉的外用并非人人适合——体质偏热、容易长痘的人应减少用量或去掉人参，以免局部皮肤出现"上火"反应。
中药面膜使用注意事项

中药面膜使用得当则养肤，使用不当则可能适得其反。敷面前务必彻底清洁面部，油脂和污垢会阻碍有效成分的吸收。面膜要避开眼周和唇周皮肤，这些区域的皮肤最薄、最敏感。敷面时间以15至20分钟为宜，过长反会倒吸皮肤水分。频率控制在每周2至3次，过于频繁反而增加皮肤负担。首次使用某一配方时，建议先在耳后或手腕内侧做小范围过敏测试，观察24小时无不良反应后再正常使用。最重要的是，中药面膜只是外治手段，真正想要好的皮肤，仍需与内调饮食作息相结合。皮肤问题严重者应首先寻求专业诊断，而非自行调配面膜。
中药面膜材料选择

中药面膜的效果与药材品质密切相关。应选择正规药店购买的道地药材，避免来源不明的药材粉末。研磨需尽可能细腻——粉末越细，有效成分越容易透皮吸收。自行研磨时可用中药粉碎机多次过筛，以"如面粉般细腻"为度。调配好的面膜应现调现用，不宜久放，因为中药粉末接触水和空气后容易滋生细菌、发生氧化变质。存放时需密封置于阴凉干燥处，避免受潮结块。购买成品中药面膜粉时，应注意查看配料表中是否有不必要的添加剂，纯中药配方应当只有中药成分。
温馨提示：中药面膜需要根据个人体质和皮肤状况选择，不存在"万能"的面膜方。首次使用建议做过敏测试。皮肤有严重痤疮感染、皮炎、过敏或破损时不宜敷用。建议在专业中医师辨证指导下选择适合自己体质和肤质的面膜配方。

en.text: Herbal facial masks represent an important application of TCM external therapy in the field of beauty, with a long history and solid theoretical foundation. The Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing contains numerous herbs suitable for external cosmetic use, while the Tang dynasty's Qian Jin Yao Fang and Wai Tai Mi Yao provide detailed records of "face-washing formulas" and "face-applying formulas" formulated with herbs such as Angelica dahurica, Atractylodes, and Poria. These ancient formulas have been passed down for millennia not merely because of their antiquity, but because of the underlying formulation philosophy — selecting different herbs based on the TCM pathogenesis of different skin conditions, applying pattern differentiation to external treatment. This is the true wisdom behind herbal masks.
Advantages of Herbal Masks

Compared to commercially available synthetic masks, herbal masks offer several distinct advantages. First, natural safety — herbal masks use natural botanical ingredients without chemical preservatives, fragrances, or dyes, minimizing skin irritation. Second, gentle nourishment — herbal ingredients are absorbed through the skin with mild medicinal properties that do not strip the stratum corneum or damage the skin barrier like certain chemical exfoliants. Third, root-and-symptom treatment — herbal masks do not simply cover up problems but select herbs according to the TCM pathogenesis of specific skin conditions (such as heat toxin, blood stasis, or damp turbidity), fundamentally improving skin condition from the source. Fourth, personalized formulation — the recipe can be flexibly adjusted according to each individual's constitution, skin type, and specific concerns, truly achieving customized skincare. Of course, herbal masks also have their limitations — they work relatively slowly and require consistent use before noticeable improvement is seen, a characteristic determined by the gentle nature of herbal ingredients.
Classic Herbal Mask Formulas
Among the ancient cosmetic formulas that have been passed down, several classic recipes remain widely used and validated by modern practice. They are well worth understanding.
Yu Rong San (Jade Face Powder)

Yu Rong San is a representative formula from ancient palace cosmetics, first recorded in the Qian Jin Yao Fang. It primarily consists of "white" herbs such as Angelica dahurica, Atractylodes, Poria, and White Peony — following the principle of "treating color with color," where white enters the lung, and the lung governs the skin and body hair. In clinical practice, I often use modified Yu Rong San, grinding the ingredients into an extremely fine powder to be mixed with water or honey as a mask. Angelica dahurica, being acrid, warm, and aromatic, can "nourish the skin and improve complexion" (as recorded in the Shen Nong Ben Cao Jing) and is the core ingredient of Yu Rong San. However, the furanocoumarin compounds in Angelica dahurica have photosensitizing activity — therefore, sun protection is essential after using masks containing this herb, as UV exposure may cause pigmentation rather than whitening. This is a point I must repeatedly emphasize in clinical practice.
San Bai Powder Mask

San Bai Powder is made by grinding equal parts of Angelica dahurica, Atractylodes, and Poria into powder — it is the most basic classic formula for whitening and beautifying the skin. Angelica dahurica whitens and moisturizes, Atractylodes strengthens the spleen and dries dampness, and Poria strengthens the spleen and drains dampness. The combination targets two major systems: "the spleen governs transportation and transformation" and "the lung governs the skin." When the spleen functions properly, damp turbidity does not arise, and the skin naturally becomes clean and clear; when lung qi is properly dispersed, the skin is moisturized. In practice, I suggest patients choose the mixing medium based on their skin type — honey for dry skin, milk or yogurt for oily skin, and water or floral water for normal skin — with flexible adjustments for optimal results.
Pearl Powder Mask

Pearl powder holds a distinguished place in TCM beauty practice. The Ben Cao Gang Mu records that pearl powder "when applied to the face, improves complexion; when applied to hands and feet, softens rough skin." The main components of pearl powder are calcium carbonate and various amino acids, providing excellent adsorption and nourishing effects when used externally. Patients often ask whether more expensive pearl powder is more effective. Medically speaking, the key factor is not price but particle fineness — the finer the powder, the better the absorption by the skin. Pearl powder of good quality should feel like fine flour when rubbed between fingers and dissolve instantly in water. It can be used alone or in combination with San Bai Powder, making it suitable for individuals seeking whitening with sensitive skin.
Functional Herbal Masks

For different skin concerns, herbal masks can be flexibly formulated like medicinal formulas, achieving the goal of "one formula for one skin type." Below are several functional mask recipes I commonly use in clinical practice.
Whitening Mask

en.title: Whitening Spot-Fading Mask
en.instructions:
1. Mix all powders
2. Add honey to form paste
3. Apply to face, avoid eye area
4. Rinse after 15-20 minutes
5. 2-3 times weekly
6. Whitens, fades spots, brightens skin

en.text: Acne Mask

en.title: Heat-Clearing Acne Mask
en.instructions:
1. Mix all powders
2. Add water to form paste
3. Apply to acne areas
4. Rinse after 10-15 minutes
5. 2-3 times weekly
6. Clears heat, detoxifies, treats acne

en.text: The core of acne-fighting masks lies in clearing heat, detoxifying, reducing swelling, and dispersing nodules. Coptis powder has strong heat-clearing and dampness-drying properties, providing the most direct effect on inflammatory acne with redness, swelling, and pain. However, due to its cold nature, it should not be left on for long — 10 to 15 minutes is sufficient. Honeysuckle and dandelion clear heat, detoxify, reduce swelling, and disperse nodules, making them particularly effective for pustular acne. Mung bean powder both clears heat and detoxifies while absorbing excess oil, making it an excellent base powder. It is worth noting that acne masks should not be applied for extended periods, as heat-clearing and detoxifying herbs have relatively strong transdermal activity — prolonged application may actually irritate the skin.
Moisturizing Mask

en.title: Moisturizing Skin Mask
en.instructions:
1. Mix all powders
2. Add honey and milk to form paste
3. Apply to face
4. Rinse after 15-20 minutes
5. 2-3 times weekly
6. Moisturizes, improves dryness

en.text: Dry, flaking, dehydrated skin is often not simply a matter of insufficient water but reflects "blood deficiency with wind-dryness" — blood deficiency prevents upward nourishment of the face, causing the skin to lose moisture, and blood deficiency generates wind, which in turn exacerbates dryness. Angelica sinensis tonifies blood and activates circulation, making it the core ingredient of moisturizing masks. Tremella mushroom is rich in natural plant colloids with excellent moisturizing properties — the Ben Cao Zai Xin describes it as "moistening the lung and nourishing yin." Lily bulb nourishes yin and moistens dryness, and combined with the natural humectants in honey and milk, forms a moisturizing protective film. I recommend that patients with dry skin use this mask 2 to 3 times weekly, combined with oral angelica blood-nourishing dietary therapy for more lasting results through both internal and external approaches.
Anti-Aging Mask

en.title: Anti-Aging Beauty Mask
en.instructions:
1. Mix all powders
2. Add honey to form paste
3. Apply to face
4. Rinse after 15-20 minutes
5. 1-2 times weekly
6. Anti-aging, beauty care

en.text: The TCM essence of skin aging lies in qi and blood depletion and gradual decline of kidney essence. Ginseng, known as the "king of all herbs," greatly tonifies primordial qi — when used externally, it enhances skin vitality and delays collagen loss. Angelica tonifies blood, goji nourishes yin, and together they work synergistically. Pearl powder supplies amino acids and trace elements needed by the skin. This formula is suitable for skin aged 35 and above that is beginning to show fine lines and laxity. However, it should be noted that ginseng powder is not suitable for everyone — individuals with a hot constitution or a tendency toward acne should reduce or omit the ginseng to avoid a localized "heat" reaction on the skin.
Herbal Mask Usage Precautions

Proper use of herbal masks nourishes the skin, while improper use can be counterproductive. Always thoroughly cleanse the face before applying a mask — oil and impurities block the absorption of active ingredients. Avoid the eye and lip areas, where the skin is thinnest and most sensitive. The application time should be 15 to 20 minutes — longer periods may actually draw moisture from the skin. Limit use to 2 to 3 times weekly; excessive frequency burdens the skin. When using a new formula for the first time, conduct a patch test on the inner arm or behind the ear, observing for 24 hours before normal use. Most importantly, herbal masks are only one aspect of external treatment — truly beautiful skin requires combined internal regulation of diet and lifestyle. Those with significant skin problems should first seek professional diagnosis rather than self-formulating masks.
Herbal Mask Material Selection

The effectiveness of herbal masks is closely tied to herb quality. Purchase authentic herbs from reputable pharmacies and avoid powders of unknown origin. Grinding should be as fine as possible — finer powders allow better transdermal absorption of active ingredients. When grinding at home, use a herbal grinder and sieve multiple times until the powder reaches a consistency "as fine as flour." Prepared masks should be used immediately and not stored, as herbal powders mixed with water and air are prone to bacterial growth and oxidative deterioration. Store dry powders in sealed containers in a cool, dry place, protected from moisture and clumping. When purchasing commercial herbal mask powders, check the ingredient list for unnecessary additives — a pure herbal formula should contain only herbal ingredients.

Note: Herbal masks should be selected based on individual constitution and skin condition — there is no "universal" mask formula. Perform an allergy test before first use. Avoid masks when the skin has severe acne infection, dermatitis, allergies, or open wounds. Consult a qualified TCM practitioner for pattern-differentiated guidance on selecting the most suitable mask formula for your constitution and skin type.
